e.body:
**logmu**（GitHub `logmu-org/r-logmu`，文档站 `r-logmu.logmu.org`）是 2026 年新出的 R 包，自述标题为 **「Actuarial Mortality Experience Analysis and Modelling（精算死亡率经验分析与建模）」**。可核实信息：**版本 0.1.0**、**Apache-2.0**、作者 **Tim Gordon**（ORCID 0009-0006-3087-4384）、仓库 **2026-08-31 创建、2026-09-10 仍在推送**、**9,261 KB**、主语言 **C++**（`cpp11` + **C++20**）、**Depends R ≥ 4.6.0**、Imports `datey`、`ggplot2 ≥ 4.0.0`、`Language: en-GB`；文档站 HTTP 200（17KB）实测。

能力（据 DESCRIPTION 与 README）：**①** 灵活的死亡率框架，含**时间型协变量**与**任意比例风险模型**；**②** A/E（实际/预期）分析含**置信区间与残差**及可视化；**③** 极大似然拟合、**AIC 选模型**、**协变量聚类**一条流水线完成；**④** 全程支持**权重（金额 vs 人数）**、**概率相关性加权**（例如让较早数据权重更低）与**时间型纳入条件**（例如按年龄切分经验期）；**⑤** 特别支持**邮编型社会经济死亡率模型**；**⑥** 计算用 **SIMD 向量化 + 多线程**。README 称作者已把其中原理用于**英美荷约 £1,000 亿的 longevity 交易**（**这是作者自述**，非独立核实）。⚠️ **两处如实标注**：NEWS 写 "Initial CRAN release"，但 **CRAN 包页在本次核实（2026-09-11）返回 Not Found**，即尚未正式上架；仓库 **0 star、无 topics**，尚无社区采用。

对 RIAA：**「设定与复核基础死亡率（base mortality）」是人寿、年金与养老金负债估值的第一道工序**，而 A/E 分析正是它的日常工作语言。这个包的价值不在「又一个模型」，而在**把 A/E → 模型拟合 → 选型 → 可视化做成一条流水线**，且**权重口径（金额/人数）与数据时效加权是一等公民**——这两点恰恰是学生作业里最容易做错、报告里又最容易被追问的地方。**邮编型社会经济模型**这一支在池内属于空白：池中有 [[human-mortality-db]]、[[mortalitylaws]]、[[mortsoa]]、[[cvmortalitymult]]、[[multipopulation-mortality-models]]、[[cmi-mortality-projections]]、[[mortalitytables]] 等**人群/表层面**资源，也有 [[expstudy]]、[[experienceanalysis-jl]] 一类**经验分析**工具，但**「同一张表按地区/社会经济分层调参」**这一层此前没有专门条目。姊妹包见 [[datey]]（年格日期运算，本包的依赖），公司型寿险建模见 [[lifeinsurer]]，生存模型见 [[lifecontingencies]]，公式手册见 [[ifoa-formulae-tables]]，开放教材见 [[actuarial-open-book]]。适合人寿/年金/养老金方向的作业与毕设。**核实说明**：GitHub 仓库元数据、DESCRIPTION、NEWS、README、文档站均实测；**未运行代码，未验证性能宣称**。
e.body_en:
**logmu** (GitHub `logmu-org/r-logmu`, docs at `r-logmu.logmu.org`) is a 2026 R package whose DESCRIPTION title is **"Actuarial Mortality Experience Analysis and Modelling"**. Verifiable details: **version 0.1.0**, **Apache-2.0**, author **Tim Gordon** (ORCID 0009-0006-3087-4384), repository **created 2026-08-31 and still pushed on 2026-09-10**, **9,261 KB**, primary language **C++** (`cpp11` + **C++20**), **Depends R ≥ 4.6.0**, Imports `datey` and `ggplot2 ≥ 4.0.0`, `Language: en-GB`; the docs site measured HTTP 200 (17KB).

Capabilities (from DESCRIPTION and README): **①** a flexible mortality framework with **time-based covariates** and **arbitrary proportional hazards models**; **②** A/E (actual vs expected) analysis including **confidence intervals and residuals** with visualisation; **③** maximum-likelihood fitting, **AIC-based model selection** and **covariate clustering** in a single pipeline; **④** end-to-end support for **weighting (amounts vs lives)**, **probabilistic relevance weighting** (e.g. down-weighting older data) and **time-based inclusion criteria** (e.g. sub-setting experience by age); **⑤** particular support for **postcode-based socio-economic mortality models**; **⑥** calculations using **SIMD vectorisation and multi-threading**. The README states that the author has applied these principles to **longevity transactions of c.£100Bn across the UK, US and Netherlands** (**the author’s own claim**, not independently verified). ⚠️ **Two honest caveats**: NEWS says "Initial CRAN release" but the **CRAN package page returned Not Found at this check (2026-09-11)**, i.e. not yet formally published there; the repository has **0 stars and no topics** and no community adoption yet.

For RIAA: **setting and reviewing base mortality is the first step in valuing life, annuity and pension liabilities**, and A/E analysis is the everyday language of that work. This package’s value is not "yet another model" but **turning A/E → model fitting → selection → visualisation into one pipeline**, with **weighting conventions (amounts vs lives) and data-recency weighting as first-class citizens** — precisely the two things students most often get wrong in assignments and are most often challenged on in reports. Its **postcode-based socio-economic models** fill a gap in this corpus: it holds population/table-level resources such as [[human-mortality-db]], [[mortalitylaws]], [[mortsoa]], [[cvmortalitymult]], [[multipopulation-mortality-models]], [[cmi-mortality-projections]] and [[mortalitytables]], plus experience-analysis tools such as [[expstudy]] and [[experienceanalysis-jl]], but **"adjusting one table by region and socio-economic stratum"** had no dedicated entry. Sister package: [[datey]] (annual-grid date arithmetic, a dependency of this package); company life modelling: [[lifeinsurer]]; survival models: [[lifecontingencies]]; formulae handbook: [[ifoa-formulae-tables]]; open textbooks: [[actuarial-open-book]]. Suits life/annuity/pension assignments and dissertations. **Verification note**: GitHub repository metadata, DESCRIPTION, NEWS, README and the docs site were all measured; **the code was not run and performance claims were not verified**.
